IPL Power Ranking

Strang problem #5 — “linear equations + team ranking” — reframed from American college football onto 19 seasons of the Indian Premier League. Eleven mandated linear-algebra stages, each with its formula, its measured numbers and its figure.

Stage list, verbatim from the course: 1. REAL-WORLD DATA, 2. MATRIX REPRESENTATION, 3. MATRIX SIMPLIFICATION, 4. STRUCTURE OF THE SPACE, 5. REMOVE REDUNDANCY, 6. ORTHOGONALIZATION, 7. PROJECTION, 8. PREDICTION / APPROXIMATION, 9. PATTERN DISCOVERY, 10. SYSTEM SIMPLIFICATION, 11. FINAL APPLICATION OUTPUT.

Open blocker — not answered

No instructor answer is recorded anywhere in this repository. The question that gates the whole project is:

“Strang problem 5 in the projects book is Linear equations + college football team ranking. May I keep Strang's mathematics and rank IPL teams instead, using the mandated 11-stage LA workflow and the 1,243-match Cricsheet dataset? Or must I submit the book's task list on college football data?”

If the answer is the book's task list is mandatory, the IPL reframe is not permitted, the uniqueness argument behind this problem choice disappears, and the code on this page would be discarded rather than adapted. The build was authorised by the repository owner so that the question can be asked against a working demo. That authorisation is not an instructor answer.

The eleven mandated stages

Order is the guidelines' own. Matrix Simplification is stage 3 and Structure of the Space is stage 4 — the pair was transposed in this project's documents for two full runs and only adversarial review caught it, so the terminal walkthrough and tests/test_demo.py both pin the banners to ascending order.

decided             = matches with a `winner` field      -> the Colley dataset
run margin          = decided AND margin_runs is present -> the Massey dataset
wicket only         = decided AND margin_runs absent     -> Colley dataset only

Stage 2 — MATRIX REPRESENTATION

Mathematical principleone match is one linear equation in 15 unknowns

Formula

for match i with winner w and loser l:
    A[i, w] = +1    A[i, l] = -1    A[i, j] = 0 otherwise
    b[i] = +margin_runs  if the first-listed team won, else -margin_runs

predicted margin for match i   =   A[i] . x   =   x[winner] - x[loser]

Stage 3 — MATRIX SIMPLIFICATION

Mathematical principleGauss-Jordan reduction finds the rank: the number of independent facts

Formula

RREF by Gauss-Jordan elimination with partial pivoting, one column at a time:
  1. find the largest |entry| in column c below the current pivot row
  2. if it is <= tol, column c is FREE - move on, no pivot taken
  3. swap that row up, divide the row by the pivot (pivot becomes exactly 1)
  4. subtract factor * pivot_row from EVERY other row, including those ABOVE

reducing above as well as below is what makes the form REDUCED: each
pivot column becomes a column of the identity.

Stage 4 — STRUCTURE OF THE SPACE

Mathematical principlerank + nullity is the whole dimension count, and the missing direction has a name

Formula

rank(A) + nullity(A) = n = 15          the rank-nullity theorem
nullity(A) = n - rank(A) = 15 - 14 = 1

A @ 1 = 0   because every row of A has one +1 and one -1 and
             13 zeros, so every row sums to zero:
             (A @ 1)_i = 1 - 1 + 0 + ... + 0 = 0

consequence: A @ (x + c*1) = A @ x for every c, so x and x + c*1 fit
identically well. ONLY DIFFERENCES OF STRENGTH ARE IDENTIFIABLE.

Verdictrank(A) = 14 and nullity(A) = 1, and the missing direction is the constant vector: A @ ones is exactly zero. Adding the same number to every team changes no predicted margin, so this problem identifies only DIFFERENCES. The gauge (zero-sum, or anchored on one team) is a choice, and it has to be stated.

Stage 5 — REMOVE REDUNDANCY

Mathematical principle14 of 558 equations are independent; the other 544 are combinations of them

Formula

basis of the row space = the rows Gauss-Jordan promoted to PIVOTS.
they are linearly independent (a nontrivial combination of reduced-
echelon rows cannot vanish) and MAXIMAL (every row not chosen was
eliminated by them, so each is a combination of them).

for this A: 14 pivot rows out of 558.  544 rows are redundant.

Stage 6 — ORTHOGONALIZATION

Mathematical principleorthogonalise, but know WHICH space: Col(A) and Row(A) are not the same object

Formula

TWO SPACES, and this project once conflated them:

  Col(A)  subset of  R^558 :  thin QR of A gives Q of shape (558, 15).
                        15 orthonormal columns spanning a 15-dim space
                        that CONTAINS the 14-dim Col(A). column 15 is an
                        orthogonal completion: it sees nothing of A.

  Row(A)  subset of  R^15  :  Gram-Schmidt on the 14 pivot rows gives
                        Q of shape (14, 15) - a genuine orthonormal basis
                        of Row(A), in a different space, with a different shape.

Gram-Schmidt step k:  v_k <- v_k - sum_j (q_j . v_k) q_j ;  q_k = v_k/||v_k||

VerdictTwo orthogonalisations, two different spaces. Thin QR orthogonalises the columns of A and gives a 558 x 15 matrix in R^558 whose 15th direction is outside Col(A) entirely; Gram-Schmidt on the pivot rows gives the (14, 15) orthonormal basis of Row(A) in R^15. They are not interchangeable, and an earlier write-up in this project said they were.

Stage 7 — PROJECTION

Mathematical principleleast squares IS the orthogonal projection of b onto Col(A)

Formula

x_hat = argmin_x ||A x - b||   is   the orthogonal projection of b
onto Col(A). So:

    b        = A x_hat  +  r          (exactly, by construction)
    r        = b - A x_hat             the residual
    r . q_j  = 0  for every q_j spanning Col(A)   <- the normal equations

equivalently  A' r = 0, i.e. r is in the LEFT null space of A.

Measured

VerdictLeast squares is a projection, not a curve fit. b splits exactly into A x_hat plus a residual of norm 963.42 runs, and that residual is perpendicular to every direction in Col(A). It is 6.8 times longer than the part that was projected, which is why the fit statistic in stage 8 is negative.

Stage 8 — PREDICTION / APPROXIMATION

Mathematical principleleast squares minimises the residual; the negative R-squared is the missing intercept, and A @ 1 = 0 is why

Formula

the normal equations   A' A x = A' b

rank-deficient, so there is no unique x - only the class x + c*1. Three
routes, three ways of handling the null direction:

  lstsq(A, b)                        SVD; truncates the zero singular value
  lstsq(A'A, A'b)                    the textbook route; A'A is ALSO rank 14
  solve(A'A + 1*1', A'b)             nonsingular: 1*1' IS the null direction

R^2 = 1 - SS_res / SS_tot, and SS_tot has TWO legitimate denominators:
  centred    SS_tot = sum (b - mean(b))^2   -> the standard R^2
  uncentred  SS_tot = sum b^2               -> correct only if b is centred
they disagree in SIGN on this data, so both are reported.

and the centred one is negative for a STRUCTURAL reason: every row of A
sums to zero, so A x has mean zero, while mean(b) = +18.04. The model
cannot represent a constant at all. Adding the one column A was never
allowed - a constant - moves centred R^2 from -0.2103 to +0.0181. The
rank deficiency of stage 4 IS the negative R^2 of stage 8.

Stage 9 — PATTERN DISCOVERY

Mathematical principlethe dominant eigenvector of a non-negative symmetric matrix is real, simple, positive

Formula

Colley's model says RANK, not margin: pull a team's rating toward the
average of the teams it beat, in proportion to how often it met them.

    M r = lam1 r        with   M = W + W' + C
      W[i,j] = wins by i over j        C[i,j] = matches between i and j

M is symmetric and entrywise non-negative, so by Perron-Frobenius the
leading eigenpair is real, simple and STRICTLY POSITIVE.

power method:   r <- M r / ||M r||      ||M r|| estimates lam1

Stage 10 — SYSTEM SIMPLIFICATION

Mathematical principlethe eigenvalues of A'A are the squared singular values: the 15x15 is A rotated

Formula

SVD:   A = U diag(sigma) V'      ->  A'A = V diag(sigma^2) V'

so the 15x15 symmetric normal-equation matrix carries exactly the same
information as the 558x15 A: it is A, rotated and squared. The tiny
eigenvalue is where the rank deficiency went.

   A' A is symmetric by construction:  (A'A)' = A'A   always, for any A.

Stage 11 — FINAL APPLICATION OUTPUT

Mathematical principletwo models, two datasets, one disagreement that is the finding

Formula

claim 1: the margin model does not work.
    centred R^2 = -0.2103 WITHOUT an intercept, +0.0181 WITH one.
    the negative value is structural: A @ 1 = 0 forbids a constant,
    so A x has mean 0 while mean(b) = +18.04, and the fit sits 17.30
    runs low on every match. stage 4's gauge freedom IS stage 8's R^2.
    winner accuracy 55.02% against a majority-class baseline of 77.96%
    -> NEGATIVE skill. max|t| = 1.20: not one coefficient at 2 sigma.

claim 2: the reason is measured, on one scale.
    residual spread  ||r|| / sqrt(m) = 40.79 runs unexplained
    fitted spread    std(A x)        =  5.98 runs of team signal
    ratio 6.82x - the unexplained part dwarfs the explained part
    corr(games played, |x|) = -0.663: short history -> extreme coefficient

claim 3: win/loss carries what the margin throws away.
    the Colley-style Perron eigenvector of W + W' + C reproduces the
    official points table; the margin fit does not. (Colley's 2002 paper
    solves a different, linear system, so the attribution is loose.)

significance:  t_i = x_i / se_i,   se from sigma^2 (A'A + 11')^-1,
                            sigma^2 = ||r||^2 / (m - rank) = ||r||^2 / 544

divergence:    Spearman between the three orderings, joined BY TEAM NAME.

VerdictThe margin model does not work, and the headline negative R^2 is not the reason people first think. Centred R^2 is -0.2103 without an intercept and +0.0181 with the one column A was never allowed to have: the model cannot fit the +18.04-run mean margin at all, because A @ 1 = 0. That is stage 4's gauge freedom showing up in stage 8, and correcting it still leaves no signal. Accuracy 55.0% against a 78.0% majority-class baseline is NEGATIVE skill. The reason is measured on one scale: 40.78 runs of unexplained margin against 5.98 runs of fitted signal, a ratio of 6.82. Frequency balancing was tried and made it worse, max|x| 17.43 -> 25.64. Win/loss, which is what the official table actually uses, reproduces it at Spearman +0.939; margin manages +0.093.

One number, two denominators

R² is 1 - SSres / SStot, and SStot has two legitimate denominators that disagree in sign on this data. Only the centred one is the standard coefficient of determination.

denominatorSStotR²reading
sum (b - mean(b))2 — centred766,931.3-0.2103the standard R²: the model is worse than predicting the mean margin
sum b2 — uncentred948,444.0+0.0214correct only when the outcome is already mean-centred; read alone it suggests the model explains 2% of the variation
add one constant column — with intercept753,087.7 (SSres)+0.0181the column A was never allowed. The negative value was structural; correcting it still leaves no signal
Why all three are printed

The sign flips between the denominators because 948,444 > 766,931: the uncentred ratio is smaller, so the subtraction leaves a small positive number. Quoting only +0.0214 would be the same class of error as the two wrong dataset counts this project had already produced.

And the centred -0.2103 has a cause that is structural, not statistical: every row of A sums to zero, so A x has mean zero while mean(b) = 18.0358 runs. The fit is 17.30 runs low on every match by construction. Adding the constant column A @ 1 = 0 forbids lifts the centred value to +0.0181 — a real improvement, and still no signal. Stage 4's rank deficiency and stage 8's R² are one argument, not two.

The finding

Three claims, all measured against the committed snapshot by the run that generated this page. Massey (1997) and Colley (2002) are published methods; no published source reports these coefficient vectors, standard errors, held-out accuracy or rank correlations for IPL data, so the numbers below are new measurements rather than a reconstruction.

Claim 1. The margin model does not work — and the first reason is structural, not statistical

Treating every IPL match as an equation in which the difference in team strength equals the run margin gives centred R² = -0.2103. That negative value is not primarily a statement about noise: every row of A sums to zero (A @ 1 = 0, proved in stage 4), so A x has mean zero while mean(b) = 18.0358 runs. The fit sits 17.30 runs low on every match by construction. Adding the one constant column A was never allowed lifts centred R² to +0.0181 — a real improvement, and still no signal. Winner accuracy is 55.0% against a majority-class baseline of 78.0%: always naming the first-listed team beats the fit, so the model has negative skill. And not one of the 15 coefficients is distinguishable from zero at 2σ (max |t| = 1.20).

Claim 2. The reason is measured, and the two sides are on one scale

Per match, ||r|| / sqrt(m) = 40.78 runs of margin are left unexplained, while the fitted margins themselves vary by only std(A x) = 5.98 runs — a ratio of 6.82×. Least squares weights every match equally, so a franchise with a short history is decided by a handful of rows: corr(games played, |x|) = -0.663. (The earlier write-up compared std(b), a data spread that includes the +18-run level, against std(x), a coefficient spread, and called the ratio a signal-to-noise figure. Both quantities are real; that ratio was not defined.)

Claim 3. Win/loss carries the information the margin throws away

The Colley-style Perron eigenvector of W + W' + C on the same fixture graph reproduces the official all-time points table at Spearman +0.939, while the margin model — which uses information the official table ignores — manages +0.093. The two models are uncorrelated with each other (0.000). Colley's 2002 paper solves a different, linear system, so the attribution is loose and is stated as loose here.

The held-out split, and why its number carries a caveat

Reported with its defect attached

Training on the first 16 seasons and scoring on the last 3 gives winner accuracy 43.2% and RMSE 46.71 runs against 35.35 for the single training-mean constant.

But the split is degenerate, and so is part of the training window. The share of run-margin matches won by the first-listed team sits between 0.44 and 0.67 across 2007/08–2017, then is exactly 1.000 for every season from 2018 onwards — nine consecutive seasons, including 2024, 2025 and 2026, which are the three test seasons. The archive's team-ordering convention changed. The test target never varies, and six of the sixteen training seasons are degenerate too. This is not a clean out-of-sample estimate; the number is reported rather than dropped, and the defect is reported with it.

The refuted hypothesis

Reported, not hidden

An inherited build audit predicted that weighting each match by 1/(games(t1) + games(t2)) would stop the short-history franchises from dominating the fit. Measurement refutes it. Ordinary least squares gives max|x| = 17.43 runs; the frequency-balanced fit gives max|x| = 25.64 runs, and R² (centred) slips from -0.2103 to -0.2113.

The diagnosis is right and the proposed repair inverts it. A thin franchise's extremity is caused by having five run-margin matches, and those five matches are exactly what the weight divides by — so balancing amplifies the very rows it was meant to discount. Fewer games is a reason to trust a franchise's results less, not more.

What was excluded, and why it is stated here

Exclusions, counted

25 of 1,243 matches carry no winner field at all — 16 decided by a Super Over eliminator and 9 abandoned. They belong to neither model. The count is here rather than in a footnote because silently dropping 2% of a dataset reads as cherry-picking.

660 of 1,243 decided matches carry a wicket margin and no run figure at all. Converting them into run equivalents would require a runs-per-wicket constant that no source in this repository supplies. Inventing one to fill the gap is forbidden, so the project runs two honest models on two different datasets instead: least squares on the 558 run margins, and a Colley eigenvector on all 1,218 decided matches. Their disagreement is the finding.

Not attempted, by decision: recency weighting (a named “what next”, not part of this deliverable), and the residual-SVD stretch variant. Not merged: Gujarat Lions into Gujarat Titans, or Deccan Chargers into Sunrisers Hyderabad — either merge changes n from 15 and invalidates every dimension and every measured figure downstream.

The joined table

Official all-time points (2 per win, all 19 seasons) with both models annotated onto it. The join is on team, never on row position: the official table arrives sorted by points and every fitted vector in this project is in alphabetical team order, and comparing them positionally has already produced one wrong measurement in this project. rank_movement is massey_rank - official_rank, so a positive entry means the margin fit ranks that franchise worse than the official table does.

what the SHA-256 covers
deterministic manifest of extracted files: sorted '<relpath>:<size>' lines

The downloaded ipl_json.zip is not retained on this machine, only its extracted contents, so the archive's own SHA-256 could not be computed. This hash covers instead a deterministic manifest of the extracted file set: every *.json file under ipl_json/, named by its path relative to ipl_json/, sorted lexicographically, hashed as the UTF-8 concatenation of '<relpath>:<size_in_bytes>' lines each terminated by a newline. It is a check on the extracted snapshot, not a substitute for the archive digest. Re-running the builder on the same extraction reproduces it; adding, editing or deleting any file changes it.

Licence position

No licence term asserted

Undetermined for the match data, and deliberately not asserted. No licence statement for Cricsheet match data was found on cricsheet.org; the site's /licence/ path returns 404. The only explicit ODC-BY statement on the site covers the separate Register dataset, not match data. Four third-party sites assert ODC-BY 1.0 for match data, which is corroboration but not proof, because none of them is the primary source. Attribution is therefore by file name and URL only: ipl_json.zip from https://cricsheet.org/downloads/ipl_json.zip, Cricsheet JSON format version 1.2.0.

Attribution, precisely and nothing more: the archive ipl_json.zip from https://cricsheet.org/downloads/ipl_json.zip, Cricsheet JSON format version 1.2.0, retrieved 2026-10-02 UTC. If asked in the viva, the answer is exactly this: no licence statement for the match data was read from the primary source, so none is claimed.

What you must do by hand

Six items, the first one gating

Everything below is outside what the code can do for you.

  1. Ask the instructor the blocker question above, and record the answer — who, when, in what form — before relying on this build. A written reply is preferred; a verbal answer must be confirmed in writing. GATING.
  2. State the licence position as read, not as assumed: Cricsheet's primary site carries no licence statement for the match data and its licence path returns 404, so no term is asserted here.
  3. Confirm the snapshot provenance by rebuilding it with python ipl-power-ranking/scripts/build_snapshot.py and checking the reported manifest hash against data/provenance.json.
  4. Rehearse the viva answers, starting with the two questions this build was corrected to answer honestly: why a margin model cannot fit the dataset's mean margin, and what the majority-class baseline does to a 55% accuracy claim.
  5. Decide whether to present the all-time official table or a per-season one, and say which out loud during the demo — the ambiguity was flagged as a viva risk.
  6. Record the released answer, or the reopen decision, in docs/reasonix/ and add the run row to docs/reasonix/INDEX.md.
